title: Summer squash, yellow or green, frozen, cooked with butter or margarine

content.title: About
content.content: Summer squash (yellow or green) are young fruits of the zucchini plant that are flash‑frozen after harvest to retain freshness, flavor, and nutrients. Cooking them with butter or margarine adds a gentle richness and improves the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Summer squash belongs to the Cucurbitaceae family and is closely related to zucchini and other gourds.
Freezing within hours of picking preserves over 90 % of vitamin C.
Yellow and green varieties differ only in skin colour; their taste is virtually identical.
They are a staple in many Asian stir‑fry and braising dishes.
Cooking with butter or margarine increases the bioavailability of carotenoids.

items.title: Rich in vitamin A
items.content: Carotenoids that convert to vitamin A support vision, immune function, and skin health.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C is a strong antioxidant and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: Summer squash is low in calories and fat, making it suitable for weight‑controlled diets.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and blood pressure.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and contributes to satiety.

items.title: Cucurbit allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to cucurbit vegetables.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Summer squash contains oxalates, which in excess can contribute to kidney stone formation.

items.title: Added fat from cooking
items.content: Using large amounts of butter or margarine can make the dish calorie‑dense.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Quickly sauté the frozen squash in butter or margarine, add it to stews, soups, or serve as a side dish. It pairs well with garlic, fresh herbs (parsley, dill), and light sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen squash in a freezer at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. Once thawed, use within 1–2 days and do not refreeze.
